intro.text: 今天的主线可以概括为「平台政策」与「工具栈之争」两条。OpenAI 那边动作密集——Sottiaux 宣布 Plus 恢复 5 小时限额，又放话 DevDay 2026 将是史上最好，这些信号都指向 AI 产品正在从「无限慷慨」走向「可持续运营」。另一边，agent 原生工具在抢地盘：Replit 的 Masad 说 Agent 已取代 Claude CoWork，Steinberger 喊出「要摆脱不能用 prompt 改动的软件」。底层的手艺也没停——Madhu Guru 讲评测的「鉴别力」，Garry Tan 给出一套反自欺的实验循环，Levie 则把「系统记录」推到了 agent 时代的聚光灯下。

sections.title: OpenAI 的政策与产品信号 / OpenAI: Policy & Product Signals
sections.desc: OpenAI 从「无限慷慨」转向「可持续运营」——Plus 恢复 5 小时限额，同时高调预告 DevDay 2026。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux (Codex & ChatGPT) announces a policy shift that will hit millions of Plus users: the 5-hour daily usage limit is coming back tomorrow, across ChatGPT Work and Codex.

He gives two reasons. On the company side, the cap 'smoothens the load on compute' so the plan can stay generous on weekly usage. On the user side, casual Plus users often 'accidentally eat through their whole week's usage' and end up confused — a bad experience.

Notably, Pro ($100) and Pro ($200) plans keep unlimited hours for now. With 9223 likes, it's the feed's most-engaged post, and a clear signal that OpenAI is shifting from infinite generosity toward sustainable operations.
original: Tomorrow we will bring back the 5h limit for Plus accounts across ChatGPT Work and Codex. I had mentioned this a while ago, but then postponed it. This is necessary as (a) the 5h limit allows us to smoothen the load on our compute, allowing to keep the plan generous in terms of weekly usage and (b) users on the Plus plan are relatively casual and new users, but then also just accidentally eat through their whole weeks usage and then are confused, making it not a great experience. We are for the upcoming months keeping the 5h limit not enabled for Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions.

rewrite: OpenAI 负责 Codex & ChatGPT 的 Thibault Sottiaux 宣布了一项将影响数百万 Plus 用户的政策调整：明天起，ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 恢复 5 小时的每日使用上限。
他给了两个理由。对公司来说，上限能「平滑计算负载」，让套餐在周使用量上保持慷慨；对用户来说，Plus 用户多是轻度或新用户，往往「不小心就把一周的额度烧光」然后陷入困惑——体验并不好。
值得注意的是，Pro（$100）和 Pro（$200）套餐暂时不限时。9223 个赞让它成为今天 feed 里互动最高的一条，也是一个清晰信号：OpenAI 正在从「无限慷慨」转向「可持续运营」。
original: 明天我们将在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 上为 Plus 账户恢复 5 小时限额。这件事我之前提过，但后来推迟了。这是必要的，因为 (a) 5 小时限额能让我们平滑计算负载，从而让套餐在周使用量上保持慷慨；(b) Plus 用户大多是轻度用户和新用户，但也会不小心把一周的额度烧光，然后感到困惑，体验并不好。接下来的几个月里，Pro $100 和 Pro $200 订阅不会启用 5 小时限额。

rewrite: The same day, Sottiaux sets expectations high for OpenAI's developer conference: 'OpenAI DevDay 2026 will be our best DevDay in the history of the company. It will not be close.'
It's a bold, unhedged claim from someone on the inside — the kind of signal that usually precedes a big product or research reveal. With 1869 likes, developers are clearly leaning in.
original: OpenAI DevDay 2026 will be our best DevDay in the history of the company. It will not be close.

rewrite: 同一天，Sottiaux 又把开发者大会的预期拉满：「OpenAI DevDay 2026 将是公司历史上最好的一届 DevDay。而且不是险胜。」
这是内部人士抛出的、毫不保留的大话——这种信号通常预示着一场重磅产品或研究的发布。1869 个赞，开发者显然都竖起了耳朵。
original: OpenAI DevDay 2026 将是公司历史上最好的一届 DevDay。而且不是险胜。

sections.title: Agent 原生工具栈之争 / The Agent-Native Stack Wars
sections.desc: agent 原生工具在抢地盘——Replit 的 Masad 说 Agent 已取代 Claude CoWork，Steinberger 喊出要摆脱不能用 prompt 改动的软件。

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad makes a concrete competitive claim: 'Replit Agent completely replaced Claude CoWork in my day-to-day work.'

His reasoning is specific — Replit Agent is 'much more persistent and fastidious,' and 'uses code/software more effectively to complete tasks.' In other words, the differentiator isn't raw model capability, but how well the agent persists through long, multi-step work and actually writes and runs code.
It's a notable signal in the coding-agent race: the winning edge is shifting from the underlying model toward the agent harness around it.
original: True. Replit Agent completely replaced Claude CoWork in my day-to-day work. It's much more persistent and fastidious, and it uses code/software more effectively to complete tasks.

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 抛出一个具体的竞争性说法：「Replit Agent 已经完全取代了我日常工作中的 Claude CoWork。」
他的理由很具体——Replit Agent「更持久、更一丝不苟」，而且「能更有效地用代码/软件来完成任务」。换句话说，差异化不在模型本身的原始能力，而在 agent 能否在漫长的多步工作中保持状态、并且真正去写代码、跑代码。
这是 coding agent 赛道上一个值得注意的信号：制胜点正在从底层模型，转向它外面那层 agent 框架。
original: 没错。Replit Agent 已经完全取代了我日常工作中的 Claude CoWork。它更持久、更一丝不苟，而且能更有效地用代码/软件来完成任务。

rewrite: OpenClaw's Peter Steinberger distills a growing sentiment into one line: 'We need to get away from software that we can't change with a prompt.'

It's a thesis about the next phase of software — tools that behave more like malleable agents you can steer with instructions, rather than rigid products with fixed UIs. 2423 likes makes it one of the most-resonant posts in the feed, suggesting the idea has crossed from niche to mainstream.
original: We need to get away from software that we can't change with a prompt.

rewrite: OpenClaw 的 Peter Steinberger 把一种正在升温的情绪浓缩成一句话：「我们需要摆脱那些不能用 prompt 来改动的软件。」
这是一个关于软件下一阶段的论点——工具应该更像可塑的 agent，能用指令来驾驭，而不是界面固定的僵硬产品。2423 个赞让它成为 feed 里共鸣最高的帖子之一，说明这个想法已经从边缘走向主流。
original: 我们需要摆脱那些不能用 prompt 来改动的软件。

sections.title: 评测与建造的手艺 / The Craft of Evals & Building
sections.desc: 底层的手艺没停——评测的「鉴别力」、以及一套反自欺的实验循环，成为今天最可落地的方法论。

rewrite: Meta's Sr Director of AI Madhu Guru continues his 'How to build great evals' series with part 8, on the discriminatory property of evals: a good eval is only useful when it can separate AI systems that are meaningfully different.

His example is blunt — five systems scoring 94, 93, 95, 94, 92, when you already know two are substantially better. 'The eval is bad cos it doesn't tell you that.' It's like giving a fifth-grade math test to PhDs: everyone aces it and you've learned nothing about who's smartest.

The fix isn't to make evals arbitrarily hard — then everyone fails and you're not measuring what your systems are meant for. The sweet spot is realistic + difficult + sensitive to differences in capability. And he ends with a warning: over time, good evals saturate as your harness and models improve.
original: How to build great evals - part 8. The discriminatory property of evals. A hill-climbing eval is useful when it can separate AI systems that are meaningfully different. It's like giving a fifth-grade math test to a group of PhDs - everyone aces it and you've learned nothing about who is the smartest. That doesn't mean making evals arbitrarily hard. Then everyone fails and you're not measuring what your systems are meant for. The sweet spot for an eval is: Realistic + difficult + sensitive to differences in capability. Over time, your good evals will saturate as your harness and underlying models improve.

rewrite: Meta 的 AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru 继续他的「如何构建好的评测」系列，第 8 部分讲评测的「鉴别力」：一个评测只有在能区分「真正有差异的 AI 系统」时才有用。
他的例子很直白——五个系统分别得 94、93、95、94、92 分，而你已经知道其中两个明显更强。「这个评测是烂的，因为它没告诉你这一点。」就像给一群博士发五年级数学卷子：人人都满分，你对谁最聪明一无所知。
解法不是把评测做得无限难——那样人人都挂，你也没测到系统本来的用途。评测的甜点区是：真实 + 有难度 + 对能力差异敏感。他还留下一个提醒：随着你的框架和底层模型进步，好评测会逐渐饱和。
original: 如何构建好的评测 - 第 8 部分。评测的鉴别力属性。一个爬山式评测只有在能区分「真正有差异的 AI 系统」时才有用。就像给一群博士发五年级数学卷子——人人都满分，你对谁最聪明一无所知。这并不意味着把评测做得无限难。那样人人都挂，你也没测到系统本来的用途。评测的甜点区是：真实 + 有难度 + 对能力差异敏感。随着你的框架和底层模型进步，好评测会逐渐饱和。

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan posts a five-step loop for building in the age of AI: form a view, turn it into an artifact or experiment, put it in contact with reality, read the result without self-deception, revise and run again.

It's a compact distillation of the scientific method for founders — and notably, 'read the result without self-deception' is the step most people skip. With 421 likes, it clearly landed as one of the day's most-shared pieces of builder advice.
original: Form a view. Turn it into an artifact or experiment. Put it in contact with reality. Read the result without self-deception. Revise and run again.

rewrite: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan 发了一条 AI 时代的五步建造循环：形成观点，把它变成一个产物或实验，让它接触现实，不自我欺骗地读取结果，修正后再跑一次。
这是科学方法给创始人的精炼版——而且值得注意的是，「不自我欺骗地读取结果」恰恰是大多数人会跳过的那一步。421 个赞，它显然成了今天被转发最多的建造者建议之一。
original: 形成观点。把它变成产物或实验。让它接触现实。不自我欺骗地读取结果。修正后再跑一次。

sections.title: 系统记录与企业 AI / Systems of Record & Enterprise AI
sections.desc: Box CEO Levie 把「系统记录」推到 agent 时代的聚光灯下——治理与合规反而更重要，ZDR 则是 AI 扩散的隐形推手。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie makes the case that systems of record (CRM, ERP, and the rest) have never mattered more than in a world where AI agents do 100X more work on these platforms than people ever did.

Agents will query the data, process tasks, execute workflows, and collaborate with human and agent users — which means governance, reliability, security, access controls, and business logic become more critical than ever. He points to the 'OpenAI Hugging Face incident' as 'a small peek' at what happens when agents run around trying to execute goals.

But the opportunity only flows to systems of record that ship the right product experiences, APIs, and business models for agents. His verdict: 'Huge moment of opportunity and disruption right now in all of software.'
original: Systems of record have never been more important than in a world where you have AI agents that will do 100X more work on these platforms than people ever did. Agents will be querying the data in these systems, processing tasks, executing workflows, collaborating with human and agent users, and more. Thus, the governance, reliability, security, access controls, and business logic remain critical more than ever — the OpenAI Hugging Face incident is just a small peek into what the future will look like with agents running around trying to execute on their goals. But this only works for the systems of record that respond with the right product experiences, APIs, and business models to support agents on and off their platform executing in these systems. Huge moment of opportunity and disruption right now in all of software.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 提出一个观点：在一个 AI agent 会在这些平台上做「比人类多 100 倍」工作的世界里，系统记录（system of record，如 CRM、ERP 等）比以往任何时候都更重要。
agent 会查询这些系统里的数据、处理任务、执行工作流、与人类和 agent 用户协作——这意味着治理、可靠性、安全、访问控制和业务逻辑比以往更加关键。他拿「OpenAI Hugging Face 事件」举例，说这只是 agent 四处跑着执行目标时未来会是什么样子的「冰山一角」。
但机会只会流向那些能提供正确产品体验、API 和商业模式来支持 agent 的系统记录。他的结论是：「当下整个软件行业正处于一个巨大的机会与颠覆时刻。」
original: 在一个 AI agent 会在这些平台上做比人类多 100 倍工作的世界里，系统记录比以往任何时候都更重要。agent 会查询这些系统里的数据、处理任务、执行工作流、与人类和 agent 用户协作等等。因此，治理、可靠性、安全、访问控制和业务逻辑比以往更加关键——OpenAI Hugging Face 事件只是 agent 四处跑着执行目标时未来会是什么样子的冰山一角。但这只适用于那些能提供正确的产品体验、API 和商业模式来支持 agent 在其平台内外执行任务的系统记录。当下整个软件行业正处于一个巨大的机会与颠覆时刻。

rewrite: In a second post, Levie argues that zero data retention (ZDR) is 'responsible for a substantial amount of the growth of AI,' because it dramatically simplified the compliance burden companies face when handling data with subprocessors.

His logic: applied-AI vendors generally offer only ZDR models, so customers don't have to inspect each model they enable — anything else is a slow exception process. And inside enterprises, governance rules often mandate ZDR because they can't cleanly separate PII from the context window.
The stakes are stark: 'Without ZDR, AI diffusion grinds to a halt.' It's a reminder that adoption is often gated by unglamorous compliance mechanics, not just model capability.
original: It's not fully appreciated that ZDR is responsible for a substantial amount of the growth of AI, because it dramatically simplified the compliance process most companies deal with in handling data with subprocessors. The alternative path would have been a far slower adoption rate. ... most companies have internal governance requirements that say they can only use ZDR models because they have no way of explicitly separating PII and other sensitive or confidential data they put in the context window across their enterprise. ... Without ZDR, AI diffusion grinds to a halt.

rewrite: 第二条帖子里，Levie 提出零数据保留（ZDR）「是 AI 增长的重要推手」，因为它大幅简化了大多数公司在处理子处理器数据时要面对的合规流程。
他的逻辑是：应用型 AI 供应商通常只提供 ZDR 模型，这样客户就不必逐一审查自己启用的每个模型——其它任何方案都是缓慢的例外流程。而企业内部，治理规则往往强制要求 ZDR，因为它们无法清晰地分离放进上下文窗口里的 PII 和其它敏感/机密数据。
他的结论很尖锐：「没有 ZDR，AI 的扩散就会陷入停滞。」这是个提醒：采用率常常被那些不性感的合规机制卡住，而不只是被模型能力卡住。
original: 人们还没有充分意识到，ZDR 是 AI 增长的重要推手，因为它大幅简化了大多数公司在处理子处理器数据时要面对的合规流程。另一条路本会是慢得多的采用率。……企业内部大多有治理要求，只能使用 ZDR 模型，因为它们无法清晰分离放进上下文窗口里的 PII 和其它敏感/机密数据。……没有 ZDR，AI 的扩散就会陷入停滞。

sections.title: 反共识与创始人视角 / Contrarian Takes & Founder Notes
sections.desc: 两条反共识声音——hackathon 是过时的活动形式，以及创始人该如何找到自己的 VC champion。

rewrite: Builder Zara Zhang opens with a self-aware contrarian take: 'Unpopular opinion: hackathons are an outdated event format (at least the way they're traditionally held).'

She doesn't elaborate in the tweet itself, but the framing invites the follow-up: if the traditional sprint format is stale, what replaces it for actually shipping something real? With 85 likes and 27 replies, it's clearly stirring debate.
original: Unpopular opinion: hackathons are an outdated event format (at least the way they're traditionally held)

rewrite: Builder 出身的 Zara Zhang 抛出一个自嘲式的反共识观点：「不讨喜的看法：hackathon 是一种过时的活动形式（至少按它们传统的办法是）。」
她在帖子里没有展开，但这个框架本身就抛出了追问：如果传统那种冲刺形式已经过时，那真正能做出东西的替代形式是什么？85 个赞、27 条回复，显然正在挑起争论。
original: 不讨喜的看法：hackathon 是一种过时的活动形式（至少按它们传统的办法是）。

rewrite: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari offers founders a blunt piece of fundraising advice: every unconventional deal 'dies a 100 times' in venture, and it usually takes one champion sticking their neck out to steer it to the finish line.

His actionable tip: figure out who your real champion is — and arm them with whatever info they need to make your case. He adds that associates and non-voting partners are 'extraordinarily useful' here, since they're incentivized to help you and it's a good test of how they'd partner with you on your cap table.
original: Every (unconventional) deal that's officially wired dies a 100 times in venture.. It usually takes one champion sticking their neck out for the founder - and quietly steering it to the completion line. Founders it's in your benefit to figure out who your real champion is to help steer the fund dynamics and arm them with whatever info you can to make your case. This is where associates and non-voting partners are extraordinarily useful as they are incentivized to help you - and it's a good test of how they'd partner with you as they come on your cap table!

rewrite: FPV Ventures 的合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 给创始人一句直白的融资建议：每一笔正式推进的（非传统）deal 在风投里「都要死上一百次」，通常需要有一个 champion 为创始人挺身而出，悄悄把它推过终点线。
他的可操作建议是：搞清楚谁是你真正的 champion，然后把能帮你站台的所有信息都交给他们。他还补充，associate 和非投票合伙人在这里「特别有用」，因为他们有动力帮你，而且这也是一个测试——看他们上了你的 cap table 之后会怎么跟你合作。
original: 每一笔正式推进的（非传统）deal 在风投里都要死上一百次。通常需要一个 champion 为创始人挺身而出，悄悄把它推向终点线。创始人，搞清楚谁是你真正的 champion 对你有好处，能帮你驾驭基金内部的博弈，并把所有能帮你站台的信息交给他们。这正是 associate 和非投票合伙人特别有用的地方，因为他们有动力帮你——而且这也是一个测试，看他们上了你的 cap table 之后会怎么跟你合作。
